name: Utah
tagline: From Bear Lake and the Uinta lakes to Zion, Capitol Reef and Monument Valley.
intro: Utah's byways climb the Wasatch and Uinta canyons, cross the high plateaus of the south, and run through the slickrock and river country around Moab, Capitol Reef and the Four Corners. This chapter follows the Utah Scenic Byway program as written in Utah Administrative Rule R926-13, administered by the Utah Department of Transportation with the State Scenic Byway Committee; the rule lists 31 state byways, and Utah's nine national byways are assembled from them, sometimes under new names, so the state's Brian Head-Panguitch Lake road is nationally Utah's Patchwork Parkway and Highway 12 is the All-American Road. The BLM back country byways and the state's dirt-road scenic backways are listed separately because they are not part of the rule.

programs.label: Utah Scenic Byways
programs.issuer: Utah Department of Transportation and the Utah State Scenic Byway Committee

members.name: Logan Canyon Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US-89 follows the Logan River northeast from Logan between limestone walls laid down over some 500 million years, then crests above the turquoise water of Bear Lake and drops to Garden City.

members.name: Bear Lake Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A short shore road beside the turquoise water of Bear Lake, from the Idaho line through Garden City, with its summer raspberry milkshakes, to Laketown, which gave the byway its first name in 1990.

members.name: Ogden River Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 39 squeezes through the narrow quartzite gorge of Ogden Canyon, opens out at Pineview Reservoir near Huntsville and climbs toward Monte Cristo Summit at nearly 9,000 feet, where snow shuts the road each winter.

members.name: Big Cottonwood Canyon Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Fifteen miles of SR-190 from a canyon mouth minutes from downtown Salt Lake City, up through old mining country to Silver Lake and the ski resorts of Solitude and Brighton. It is protected watershed, so dogs stay home.

members.name: Little Cottonwood Canyon Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR-210 climbs a glacier-cut canyon of granite, the same stone pioneers quarried at its mouth for the Salt Lake Temple, past climbers on the walls to Alta and the summer wildflowers of Albion Basin.

members.name: Provo Canyon Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US-189 follows the Provo River up its canyon, where Bridal Veil Falls spills in two steps within sight of the road, then passes Deer Creek Reservoir and turns through Midway to Heber City, home of an old tourist railroad.

members.name: Mirror Lake Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR-150 leaves the ranch country around Kamas and climbs into the Uinta Mountains to Bald Mountain Pass at 10,715 feet, the highest paved road in Utah, among lakes and trailheads into the High Uintas Wilderness.

members.name: Morgan-Parleys Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From Morgan the road climbs past East Canyon State Park and over Big Mountain toward Parleys Canyon, on the line pioneer and Pony Express travelers took; the stretch south of Big Mountain closes half the year.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Great Salt Lake Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Legacy Parkway runs north from I-215 to Farmington with Great Salt Lake off to the west, where millions of migrating birds stop each spring and fall; since 2018 the byway reaches on to the Antelope Island marina.

members.name: Markagunt High Plateau Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR-14 climbs out of Cedar City through a narrow canyon to the 9,900-foot rim of the Markagunt Plateau, then runs east across old lava fields and aspen past Navajo Lake, which drains away through sinkholes.

members.name: Cedar Breaks Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A short, high road across the rim of Cedar Breaks, above 10,000 feet in places, past wildflower meadows and overlooks into an eroded amphitheater 2,000 feet deep. In winter it closes and becomes a groomed snowmobile trail.

members.name: Brian Head-Panguitch Lake Scenic Byway (Utah's Patchwork Parkway)
members.blurb: SR-143 climbs steeply from Parowan past Brian Head to 10,400 feet and down through aspen and lava to Panguitch Lake. It is named for the 1864 settlers who crossed the snow here on laid-down quilts.
members.note: Shown on the map as Scenic Byway 143 - Utah's Patchwork Parkway.

members.name: Kolob Fingers Road Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Five miles of red pavement from I-15 into the Kolob Canyons corner of Zion, climbing beneath the 2,000-foot walls of the parallel finger canyons to the Timber Creek Overlook.

members.name: Zion Park Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR-9 runs east from I-15 through Rockville and Springdale into Zion National Park, then climbs through the Zion-Mount Carmel Tunnel and leaves by the east entrance for Mount Carmel Junction; the park fee applies even to through traffic.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Mt. Carmel Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Sixty miles of US-89 between Kanab and the Bryce Canyon turnoff, stepping up the colored cliff bands of the Grand Staircase and following the Sevier River valley high onto the Markagunt Plateau.

members.name: Beaver Canyon Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From the old town of Beaver, Highway 153 follows Beaver Creek up into the Tushar Mountains, worn-down volcanoes, climbing 4,000 feet past small power plants and ponderosa pine to meadows below Eagle Point.

members.name: Fishlake Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR-25 leaves Highway 24 and climbs to Fish Lake, five and a half miles of trout water in a fault-dropped basin near 8,800 feet, then continues past Johnson Valley Reservoir, where the Fremont River begins.

members.name: Highway 12, A Journey Through Time Scenic Byway (Scenic Byway 12)
members.blurb: SR-12 threads the red arches of Red Canyon, passes Bryce Canyon and the canyon country of Escalante, then rides the narrow Hogback to Boulder and crosses the aspen and pine of Boulder Mountain to Torrey.

members.name: Capitol Reef Country Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR-24 follows the Fremont River from the ranch towns around Loa through the Waterpocket Fold and the orchards of Fruita, then crosses gray shale badlands under Factory Butte, with no fuel between Torrey and Hanksville.

members.name: Flaming Gorge-Uintas Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From Vernal the highway climbs through rock layers holding fossils of ancient seas and dune fields, over the Uinta forests to Flaming Gorge Dam and Manila, with bighorn sheep on the cliffs above Sheep Creek.

members.name: Indian Canyon Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US-191 links Helper and Duchesne across the colorful country between the San Rafael Swell and the Uintah Basin, through steep rock formations and stands of conifer and aspen, as one side of the Dinosaur Diamond.

members.name: The Energy Loop: Huntington and Eccles Canyons Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A loop over the Wasatch Plateau through coal country, from Fairview past Electric Lake and working mines down Huntington Canyon, where a 9,500-year-old mammoth turned up during work on the reservoir dam.

members.name: Nebo Loop Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A 38-mile forest road between Payson and Nephi that climbs from scrub oak into aspen and spruce beneath 11,928-foot Mount Nebo, passing Payson Lakes and the red hoodoos of Devils Kitchen. Snow closes it in winter.

members.name: Upper Colorado River Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR-128 follows the Colorado River upstream from Moab between red sandstone walls, past the valleys where Wagon Master and Rio Grande were filmed and the Fisher Towers below the La Sals, to the railroad ghost town of Cisco.

members.name: Potash-Lower Colorado River Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR-279 runs down the Colorado River below sandstone walls where climbers hang beside the road, past petroglyph panels and dinosaur tracks, and ends at the potash evaporation ponds 17 miles from the highway.

members.name: Dead Horse Mesa Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR-313 climbs from the Moab highway onto the mesa top, then branches to Dead Horse Point, 2,000 feet above the Colorado River, and to the Island in the Sky road ending at Grand View Point in Canyonlands.

members.name: Indian Creek Corridor Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SR-211 crosses the sage plain north of Monticello and twists down to Newspaper Rock, a cliff face crowded with old petroglyphs, then follows Indian Creek between climbers' walls and ranch land to the Needles.

members.name: Bicentennial Highway Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Built for the 1976 bicentennial, SR-95 crosses empty canyon country from Hanksville past the Henry Mountains and over the Colorado at Hite to Blanding, with no fuel or food along the way.

members.name: Trail of the Ancients Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A loop through Ancestral Puebloan country around Blanding and Bluff, from the stone bridges of Natural Bridges past the museum at Edge of the Cedars to Bluff and the ancient village sites of Hovenweep.

members.name: Monument Valley to Bluff Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US-163 comes north out of Arizona through the red spires of Monument Valley on the Navajo Nation, crosses the San Juan River on an old bridge at Mexican Hat, named for a sombrero-shaped rock, and runs on to Bluff.

members.name: Dinosaur Diamond Prehistoric Highway Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A long diamond of highways through the dinosaur country of eastern Utah and western Colorado, joining Moab, Price and Vernal by way of active dig sites, museums and Dinosaur National Monument.

members.name: Bull Creek Pass National Back Country Byway
members.blurb: A rough, single-lane dirt loop of 68 miles into the Henry Mountains, climbing nearly a mile from badlands and buttes through ponderosa and spruce to Bull Creek Pass, in country shared with a free-ranging bison herd.

members.name: Nine Mile Canyon Backway
members.blurb: From Wellington the road follows a canyon of buff cliffs where Fremont people carved and painted many rock panels and stored grain on high ledges; old telegraph poles and homestead cabins mark the later traffic.

members.name: Pony Express Trail National Back Country Byway
members.blurb: A 133-mile gravel road across the west desert on the line the Pony Express riders took in 1860 and 1861, passing the remains of relay stations every ten miles or so between bare ranges and wide basins.

members.name: Silver Island Mountains Back Country Byway
members.blurb: A 54-mile loop around the Silver Island Mountains at the edge of the Bonneville Salt Flats near Wendover, crossing the wagon ruts of the Hastings Cutoff that the Donner-Reed party followed in 1846.
members.note: Shown on the map as Silver Island Mountain National Back Country Byway.

members.name: Smithsonian Butte National Back Country Byway
members.blurb: Nine miles of back road from Rockville up out of the Virgin River bottoms to the sage flats of Big Plain, below Smithsonian Butte and with Zion's towers behind; a side road reaches the 1861 ghost town of Grafton.

members.name: Transcontinental Railroad Back Country Byway
members.blurb: Ninety miles on the hand-built 1869 Central Pacific grade, west from Golden Spike across the Great Salt Lake Desert past ghost-town foundations, earthworks and old culverts toward the Nevada line.

members.name: Kolob Reservoir Scenic Backway
members.blurb: A high back road of about 45 miles from SR-14 above Cedar City through aspen to Kolob Reservoir, then down through grassy meadows into the red and white rock of Zion's backcountry. Snow closes it in winter.
